verdicts.reason: The quote is verbatim at lines 6-7 of the ruling file ("Sam: \"sounds like you've got a good shout on what the plants should be, just do the plants code\""), the only speech of Sam the file carries. The statement — the owner ruled plants use their own plants-specific code rather than the animals code — follows from "just do the plants code" read with the same decision's "C640 stays the animals code". The note's framing (overview-and-review build session, the status page's question, unblocks req-2002 and inc-199) is all in the file, at line 3 and line 7.

The quote is verbatim at lines 5-6 (the file wraps it across two lines: "...for Plants," / "Plant Products and Other Objects (CHED-PP)."). The value C085 and the CHED-PP expansion are the file's own words, so the statement does not overreach. The confidence "inferred" is defensible but arguably loose — the ruling file states C085 outright, so against the file it is verbatim; it is only Sam's quoted speech that stops short of the code. The statement also carries the extractor's reasoning about confidence rather than being a plain fact; the reconciler should read the first sentence as the claim. Content is right, so it holds.

"C640 stays the animals code (CHED-A)." is verbatim at line 6. The statement's expansion of CHED-A to "Common Health Entry Document for Animals" is not in the file; it is a sound reading of the same decision's CHED-PP expansion, so the claim holds, but the expansion is inferred rather than quoted.

"**No new \"Submitted action required\" status.**" is verbatim at line 9, the opening of decision 2. The statement restates it exactly. The note is right that the file quotes no speech of Sam for decision 2.
Verbatim at lines 9-10: "A notification submitted with outstanding items (such as a missing health certificate) is `SUBMITTED`, like any other." The statement follows without overreaching.

Verbatim at lines 10-11: "Agreed with Syed Islam (16 Nov): a status that does not align with the notification flow is not introduced". The statement adds the year 2026 to "16 Nov", which the title line ("Ruling: Sam, 16 November 2026") supports. Correctly recorded as the decision's ground, attributed to the agreement with Syed Islam rather than to Sam's speech.

Verbatim at lines 11-12 (wrapped as "...which" / "the dashboard designs under test introduce"). The statement restates it; it does not claim any design detail, and points at the gap claim p1-018 for what the file leaves open.

Verbatim at lines 12-13 (wrapped across "Submitted action" / "required"): "This withdraws the 9 October afternoon ruling's \"Submitted action required\" status (req-902's status, req-1987's new status)". The statement is the same fact, with the two req ids the file names.

Verbatim at lines 13-14: "and the 'Action required' tag on the live-animals list (inc-131's action-required criteria)". The sentence's subject is the same "This withdraws", so the statement that the tag is withdrawn follows. Splitting it from the status withdrawal is fair: one clause, two observable facts.

Verbatim at lines 14-15: "What stays: submitting records its date and the outstanding items left at that moment (req-909), since a future banner needs them." The statement takes only the date half, which the quote says. Note for the reconciler, not a refutation: sources.json records that this "What stays" clause is replaced by ruling:sam-2026-11-19, which keeps only the submitted date — so this half survives that replacement.

The same verbatim sentence at lines 14-15 says "and the outstanding items left at that moment", so the claim holds as a reading of this file. Note for the reconciler: sources.json says ruling:sam-2026-11-19 replaces this clause and keeps only the submitted date, so this is the half the later ruling overrides; precedence is the reconciler's call, not a refutation of the extract.

The quoted sentence is verbatim at lines 15-17 (wrapped). "The notification's status tag reads 'Submitted'" is its first clause, so the statement follows. The claim is a copy fact split out of a four-fact sentence, as its note says.

The quote is verbatim at lines 15-17: "the view's action-required warning, its 'Continue' and the review's 'Upload a valid health certificate' error come out with the status (req-902, req-903, req-907) until the banner design is agreed". The statement takes the first listed item and keeps the sentence's "until the banner design is agreed" condition.

Same verbatim sentence at lines 15-17. "its 'Continue'" refers back to "the view's", so attributing the 'Continue' to the notification view is sound. The note is right that the file lists req-902, req-903 and req-907 together without saying which item belongs to which.

Same verbatim sentence at lines 15-17: "the review's 'Upload a valid health certificate' error come out with the status ... until the banner design is agreed". The statement reads "the review's" as the review page, which is the only sensible reading, and keeps the condition.

Verbatim at lines 17-18: "Orchestrator's call, applying the ruling narrowly: nothing action-required is shown until that design lands." The statement records both the rule and the file's own marking of it as the orchestrator's application rather than Sam's decision, which is exactly what the file says.

Verbatim at line 19: "\"Completed\" stays out until a real source of completion exists: none does today." The statement adds "as a notification status", which the context (decision 2 is about notification statuses) supports and does not overreach.

Gap confirmed: I read all 19 lines and the file names a "banner-style alert" (lines 11-12) and says the dashboard designs under test introduce it, but gives no wording, placement, appearance or owner for it. Empty quote is right for a gap, and the claim's point that everything taken out is conditional on that design matches lines 15-18.

Gap confirmed: the file says only "until the banner design is agreed" (line 17) and "nothing action-required is shown until that design lands" (line 18). Nothing in the file sets a trigger, condition or rule for showing anything action-required once the design lands, even though it keeps the data for a future banner (lines 14-15).

Gap confirmed: line 19 holds "Completed" out "until a real source of completion exists: none does today" and names no candidate system, event or signal that would count. The file says nothing else about completion.

Gap confirmed: decision 1 (lines 5-7) sets the code values and the preamble (line 3) says the ruling answers "the status page's question on plants' customs document code", but no page file, view, component, field or data shape appears anywhere in the 19 lines. The claim already allows for the preamble's hint, so it does not overstate the silence.

missed.statement: A notification can be submitted while items are still outstanding, such as a missing health certificate: the ruling treats such a submission as a normal submission rather than blocking it. This follows from the file calling a notification "submitted with outstanding items" and giving it the SUBMITTED status "like any other", which presupposes the submission goes through.
missed.quote: A notification submitted with outstanding items (such as a missing health certificate) is `SUBMITTED`, like any other.
missed.note: Open point for the reconciler only in so far as the file does not say what, if anything, warns the user before submitting; the extract's claim p1-005 records the resulting status but not that submission with outstanding items is permitted at all, which is the behaviour an increment has to build.
